newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt narrowly mixed in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt narrowly mixed in thin trade.

text.p: Brady bond prices ended the day narrowly mixed in extremely thin trade as market participants kept to the sidelines amid continued nervousness over the U.S. interest rate environment, market experts said.

"I think customers probably have not yet regained confidence," said Kurt Schmid, managing director of emerging markets at SBC Warburg. "I think uncertainty as to the future of the U.S. interest rate environment continues and I think investors basically continue to have a defensive strategy."
At 1630 EDT/2130 GMT, Mexican pars were off 1/4 at 70-3/8 bid while Argentine FRBs were up 3/8 at 89-5/8 bid.
Trading sources attributed the price gains on Argentine debt instruments to dealer short-covering.

Meanwhile, some market experts said a widening of yield spreads between the higher yielding emerging market debt instruments and the less risky emerging market debt is likely to continue in the weeks ahead.

"Our opinion is essentially unchanged where we expect to see, with yesterday being an exception of course, a flight to quality phenonomem," said Carlos Asillis, emerging market debt strategist at UBS Securities.

Given expectations of further increases in U.S. interest rates, Asillis said he expects that the flight to quality phenomenon will basically dictate the direction of the markets over the next several weeks.
"We think the recent tightening is only the first of a series of moves by the Fed (Federal Reserve), which when the process is done may include an increase of 75 basis points," he added.
Among the more speculative credits, market sources said reports that Ecuador postponed its $300 million bond deal due to market conditions had pressured some of the country's Brady bond instruments.
Ecuador's discount bonds were 5/8 lower at 63-5/8 bid and its IEBs ECIEB were 1/8 softer at 83-5/8.
